<file path="building-blocks/persistence/SmartDbContext.cs">
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using System;
using System.Linq;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;

namespace BuildingBlocks.Persistence;

public abstract class SmartDbContext : DbContext
{
    protected SmartDbContext(DbContextOptions options) : base(options)
    {
    }

    protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
    {
        base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder);
        
        // Enforce Snake Case convention globally if needed
        // For Postgres, it is standard. Npgsql provides a method for this, 
        // typically configured via options.UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention() in Program.cs.
    }

    public override int SaveChanges()
    {
        UpdateAuditFields();
        return base.SaveChanges();
    }

    public override Task<int> SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        UpdateAuditFields();
        return base.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
    }

    private void UpdateAuditFields()
    {
        var entries = ChangeTracker.Entries()
            .Where(e => e.State == EntityState.Added || e.State == EntityState.Modified);

        foreach (var entry in entries)
        {
            var utcNow = DateTime.UtcNow;

            var createdAtProp = entry.Properties.FirstOrDefault(p => p.Metadata.Name == "CreatedAtUtc" || p.Metadata.Name == "created_at_utc");
            if (createdAtProp != null && entry.State == EntityState.Added)
            {
                createdAtProp.CurrentValue = utcNow;
            }

            var updatedAtProp = entry.Properties.FirstOrDefault(p => p.Metadata.Name == "UpdatedAtUtc" || p.Metadata.Name == "updated_at_utc");
            if (updatedAtProp != null)
            {
                updatedAtProp.CurrentValue = utcNow;
            }
        }
    }
}

<file path="database/mongodb/ais/README.md">
# AIS MongoDB Documentation

This directory tracks the retention and schemas for the `smart_ais_raw` database.

## Architecture
- **Purpose**: A high-volume, flexible datastore capable of capturing massive provider payloads (e.g. NMEA strings, JSON feeds, XML bursts).
- **Indexing**: Designed for time-series extraction and incident reprocessing.
- **Payload Security**: No raw payloads are executed.

## Security
- Store MongoDB connection strings strictly in Vault (`secret/platform/mongodb/ais`).
- Never expose telemetry databases to the public web directly.
</file>

<file path="database/mongodb/telemetry/README.md">
# Telemetry MongoDB Documentation

This directory tracks the retention and schemas for the `smart_telemetry` database.

## Architecture
- **Purpose**: A high-volume, flexible datastore capable of capturing diverse IoT sensors (Odometer, Fuel, Engine, Temperature).
- **Indexing**: Designed for time-series extraction. Ensure indexes are mapped by `tenantId`, `vehicleReference`, and `timestampUtc`.
- **Schema Mapping**: While EF Core structurally maps the strict SQL queryable properties, the firehose of unstructured GPS tracking payloads and IoT metrics land directly here.

## Security
- Store MongoDB connection strings strictly in Vault (`secret/platform/mongodb/telemetry`).
- Never expose telemetry databases to the public web directly.
</file>

<file path="database/postgresql/ais/README.md">
# AIS PostgreSQL Documentation

This directory tracks the migrations and EF Core PostgreSQL mappings for the `smart_ais` database.

## Architecture
- **PostGIS Extensions**: Enabled via `modelBuilder.HasPostgresExtension("postgis");`.
- **GiST Indexing**: Natively implemented on spatial properties across Ports, Berths, Anchorage Areas, and Vessel Positions.
- **Optimistic Concurrency**: Enforced on all configuration elements utilizing `byte[] Version` mapped to RowVersion limits.

## Migrations
Run `dotnet ef migrations add InitialAisSchema` manually in an environment that has the .NET SDK installed. The mappings defined in `AisDbContext.cs` natively bind `NetTopologySuite` objects to their PostgreSQL representations.
</file>

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS smart_analytics;

-- ==========================================
-- DIMENSIONS
-- ==========================================

CREATE TABLE smart_analytics.dim_tenant (
    tenant_key UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id UUID NOT NULL,
    tenant_reference VARCHAR(255),
    tenant_type VARCHAR(50),
    organization_reference VARCHAR(255),
    country_reference VARCHAR(100),
    effective_from_utc TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    effective_to_utc TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    is_current BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true
);
CREATE INDEX idx_dim_tenant_id ON smart_analytics.dim_tenant(tenant_id, is_current);

CREATE TABLE smart_analytics.dim_date (
    date_key INT PRIMARY KEY, -- e.g., 20260921
    full_date DATE NOT NULL,
    day_of_month INT NOT NULL,
    day_of_week INT NOT NULL,
    week_of_year INT NOT NULL,
    month_of_year INT NOT NULL,
    month_name VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    quarter INT NOT NULL,
    year INT NOT NULL,
    is_weekend BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
    fiscal_period VARCHAR(50)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_dim_date_full_date ON smart_analytics.dim_date(full_date);

CREATE TABLE smart_analytics.dim_time (
    time_key INT PRIMARY KEY, -- e.g., 143025 (14:30:25)
    hour_of_day INT NOT NULL,
    minute_of_hour INT NOT NULL,
    second_of_minute INT NOT NULL,
    time_bucket VARCHAR(50)
);

CREATE TABLE smart_analytics.dim_vehicle (
    vehicle_key UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    vehicle_id UUID NOT NULL,
    tenant_id UUID,
    vehicle_type VARCHAR(100),
    vehicle_category VARCHAR(100),
    effective_from_utc TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    effective_to_utc TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    is_current BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true
);

# ANPR / Gate / Border Operations PostgreSQL Documentation

This directory encapsulates schema documentation, ERDs, and migration standards for the `smart_anpr` database.

## Critical Security Principle
The primary architectural design rule of this database is:
**ANPR RECOGNITION IS EVIDENCE. ANPR RECOGNITION IS NOT AUTHORIZATION.**

Gates never open directly due to an `AnprRecognitionEvent`. They open exclusively via a `GateAuthorizationDecision`.

## PostGIS Initialization
The database requires `postgis` to be active. `AnprDbContext` initializes this dependency programmatically (`modelBuilder.HasPostgresExtension("postgis");`). 

## Spatial Configurations
- All coordinates must use standard SRID `4326` (WGS 84).
- Point locations utilize `geography` types mapping accurately over Earth's curvature.

## Execution
Run `dotnet ef migrations add InitialAnprSchema` manually from a host containing the .NET 10 SDK, as the target execution environment may not possess full SDK binaries.
</file>

<file path="database/postgresql/audit/README.md">
# Enterprise Audit PostgreSQL Documentation

This directory encapsulates schema documentation, ERDs, and migration standards for the `smart_audit` database.

## Critical Ownership Principle
The Audit Service is the centralized platform audit and security-traceability service. **IT DOES NOT OWN THE BUSINESS DOMAIN.**
There are no User, Role, Declaration, Vehicle, or Payment core records here. The audit ledger exclusively holds serialized snapshots and immutable reference states (`ActorReference`, `ResourceReference`).

## Immutability
All core tables (`AuditEvent`, `AuditChange`, `AuditSecurityEvent`) are strictly append-only. 
The application MUST NOT be granted `UPDATE` or `DELETE` roles over these structures at runtime. Revisions to audits are captured via CORRECTION event insertions.

## Hash Chain
Tamper evidence is calculated continuously. Records insert a SHA-256 `IntegrityHash` derived from canonical event states and chained using `PreviousIntegrityHash`. `AuditIntegrityRecord` chunks these bounds for background validation.

## Execution
Run `dotnet ef migrations add InitialAuditSchema` manually from a host containing the .NET 10 SDK.
</file>

<file path="database/postgresql/customs/README.md">
# Customs Database Schema & Configurations

This directory manages the PostgreSQL schema definitions and migrations for the `smart_customs` database.

## Principles
- **No Hardcoded Tax Rates**: The system relies entirely on `TariffScheduleVersion`, `TariffItem`, and `CustomsRateVersion` to calculate duties. No `.NET` or `SQL` code contains "if VAT == 10%". 
- **No Siloed Data**: Domestic taxes (VAT, GST) are not automatically applied unless explicitly inserted by government configuration into the `CustomsChargeType` mapping.
- **Idempotent Operations**: The use of `IdempotencyRecord` prevents a system error or timeout from mistakenly re-charging an importer or duplicating an assessment line.

## Migration Structure
Entity Framework Migrations belong to `/src/services/Customs/Customs.Infrastructure`. Do not create raw `.sql` upgrade scripts in this folder outside of specialized tuning (like partition tuning for high-volume logs).

## Tenancy
Multi-tenant scoping ensures `TenantId` blocks cross-talk between different port systems or government instances using the platform.

## Backups
Follow the global `database/scripts/backup` standard for continuous WAL archiving and daily snapshotting to S3.
</file>

<file path="database/postgresql/declaration/README.md">
# Smart Platform Declaration Database

This directory contains the database structures, configurations, and definitions specific to the **Cargo & Customs Declaration Microservice** (`smart_declaration`).

## Governance
- **Owner:** Declaration Microservice
- **Direct Access:** Strictly forbidden from external services (e.g. Customs Assessment, Fleet, Payment, ECTN). All interactions must be through approved REST API endpoints or asynchronous Events.

## Schema Highlights
- Relies on `SmartDbContext` for centralized UTC timestamp tracking (`CreatedAtUtc`, `UpdatedAtUtc`) and auditing.
- Robust usage of PostgreSQL `NUMERIC(19,4)` for precise weight and monetary calculations.
- PostgreSQL `JSONB` applied exclusively to telemetry/extensible logging (`DetailsJson`, `ChangeSummaryJson`, `AuditEntry`).

## Versioning & Amendment Policies
- The `CustomsDeclaration` contains the mutable metadata of the transaction (Status, Dates).
- The `DeclarationVersion` acts as the root of the substantive content of the declaration. Once a version is Submitted/Accepted, it is treated as an immutable legal record. 
- Revisions are enforced via `DeclarationAmendment`, which generates a new `DeclarationVersion` rather than overwriting historical evidence.

## Deletion Policy
- `DeleteBehavior.Cascade` is used internally within the core version aggregate (e.g. Version -> Cargo -> Item).
- `DeleteBehavior.Restrict` is strictly enforced from `CustomsDeclaration` to prevent orphaned versions, decisions, submissions, and status histories.
</file>

# Fleet Database Schema & Configurations

This directory manages the PostgreSQL schema definitions and migrations for the `smart_fleet` database.

## Principles
- **Authoritative Assets Only**: Fleet creates, owns, and manages Vehicles, Trailers, and Drivers. It explicitly does **not** manage external domains (GPS pings, Customs tariffs, Payments). 
- **Assignment Concurrency**: `VehicleAssignment`, `DriverAssignment`, and `TrailerAssignment` are configured with optimistic concurrency and indexing (`StartAtUtc`, `EndAtUtc`, `Status`) to prevent double-booking physical assets.
- **Dispatch Readiness**: Dispatches are blocked by `FleetHold` active records. A Dispatch transitions to `Ready` only after all its `DispatchRequirement` entities (including external Customs Release flags sent via event) are satisfied.

## Migration Structure
Entity Framework Migrations belong to `/src/services/Fleet/Fleet.Infrastructure`. 
- No raw SQL logic is permitted to bypass EF tracking unless specifically annotated for performance index tuning.

## Backups
Standard backup rotation must apply here. Operations heavily depend on the continuity of driver credentials, active compliance metrics, and dispatch orders.
</file>

# GPS PostgreSQL Documentation

This directory tracks the migrations and EF Core PostgreSQL mappings for the `smart_gps` database.

## Architecture
- **PostGIS Extensions**: Enabled via `modelBuilder.HasPostgresExtension("postgis");`.
- **GiST Indexing**: Natively implemented on spatial properties (e.g. `Position` and `Geometry`).
- **Isolation**: Fleet entities are tracked purely via `VehicleReference` values. GPS is independent.

## Migrations
Due to the `.NET 10 SDK` constraint on the host, run `dotnet ef migrations add InitialGpsSchema` manually in an environment that has the SDK installed. The mappings defined in `GpsDbContext.cs` natively bind `NetTopologySuite` objects (`Point`, `Geometry`) to their PostgreSQL representations.
</file>

# Integration & Interoperability PostgreSQL Documentation

This directory encapsulates schema documentation, ERDs, and migration standards for the `smart_integration` database.

## Critical Ownership Principle
The primary architectural design rule of this database is:
**INTEGRATION SERVICE STORES METADATA, ROUTING, AND STATUS. IT DOES NOT OWN THE DOMAIN.**

No `CustomsAssessment`, `Vehicle`, `PaymentLedger`, or `AnprRecognition` tables exist here. The database stores strictly `IntegrationExternalReference`, `IntegrationMessage`, and `WebhookSubscription` artifacts mapping these platforms together.

## Vault Integration
`IntegrationAuthentication` strictly stores `VaultSecretPath`. Never insert tokens directly into this database.

## Execution
Run `dotnet ef migrations add InitialIntegrationSchema` manually from a host containing the .NET 10 SDK, as the target execution environment may not possess full SDK binaries.
</file>

<file path="database/postgresql/payment/README.md">
# Payment Database Schema & Configurations

This directory manages the PostgreSQL schema definitions and migrations for the `smart_payment` database.

## Principles
- **No Siloed Data**: The payment system does not replicate the structural details of a Customs Declaration or an ECTN. It strictly receives the financial obligation via an event, generates an `Invoice`, and processes a `PaymentIntent`.
- **Idempotent Operations**: The use of `IdempotencyRecord` guarantees that a customer is never double-charged due to a retry timeout.
- **Strictly Immutable Ledger**: `LedgerEntry` is the ultimate source of truth for the financial state. It is an append-only log. Updates or deletions are forbidden by design. 
- **Secret Management**: API keys and Webhook secrets are never stored directly in the `PaymentGatewayConfiguration`. Instead, a reference (like an ARN or Vault Path) is stored in `ApiKeySecretRef`.

## Migration Structure
Entity Framework Migrations belong to `/src/services/Payment/Payment.Infrastructure`. Do not create raw `.sql` upgrade scripts in this folder outside of specialized tuning.

## Tenancy
Multi-tenant scoping ensures `TenantId` blocks cross-talk between different financial configurations using the platform.

## Backups
Follow the global `database/scripts/backup` standard for continuous WAL archiving and daily snapshotting to S3. Payment databases generally require the highest level of backup retention and security mirroring.
</file>

-- =======================================================
-- DB PHASE 17 - ENTERPRISE DATABASE INDEXING
-- =======================================================

-- 1. TENANT-AWARE COMPOSITE INDEXES
-- Optimizes: WHERE TenantId = @tenantId AND Status = @status ORDER BY CreatedAt DESC

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_trip_tenant_status_created 
ON smart_analytics.fact_trip(tenant_key, trip_reference)
-- In a real scenario, this would include (tenant_key, status, created_at)
;

-- 2. PARTIAL INDEXES
-- Optimizes: queries searching only for active or pending states to reduce B-Tree size

-- Example on an 'outbox_messages' table (if it exists)
-- CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_outbox_unprocessed 
-- ON smart_integration.outbox_messages(created_at) 
-- WHERE processed_at IS NULL;

-- 3. MISSING FOREIGN KEY INDEXES
-- Optimizes: JOINs and CASCADE operations

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_dim_route_origin_key 
ON smart_analytics.dim_route(origin_key);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_dim_route_destination_key 
ON smart_analytics.dim_route(destination_key);

-- 4. BRIN INDEXES (For massive append-only tables like GPS or Audit)
-- Optimizes: sequential time-range scans on very large tables

-- CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_gps_recorded_at_brin 
-- ON smart_gps.gps_positions USING BRIN (recorded_at);

-- 5. SPATIAL GIST INDEXES (PostGIS)
-- Optimizes: Spatial bounding box and proximity queries

-- CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_gps_location_gist 
-- ON smart_gps.gps_positions USING GIST (location);

-- NOTE: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block in PostgreSQL.
</file>

<file path="database/postgresql/security/V19_001__Role_Segregation.sql">
-- =======================================================
-- DB PHASE 19 - ENTERPRISE DATABASE SECURITY HARDENING
-- ROLE SEGREGATION SCRIPT
-- =======================================================

-- IMPORTANT: This script should be run by the database cluster SUPERUSER.

-- 1. Enforce SCRAM-SHA-256 for all new passwords
SET password_encryption = 'scram-sha-256';

-- 2. Revoke default public schema grants to prevent lateral escalation
REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;
REVOKE ALL ON DATABASE smart_identity FROM PUBLIC;
REVOKE ALL ON DATABASE smart_payment FROM PUBLIC;
-- (Repeat for all DB01-DB17)

-- 3. Create explicit Migration Roles (Used by CI/CD EF Core bundle ONLY)
CREATE ROLE smart_migration_role NOLOGIN;
-- Migration role gets DDL access
GRANT CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO smart_migration_role;
-- Vault will assign dynamic scram-sha-256 passwords to this role during pipeline runs

-- 4. Create explicit Application Runtime Roles (Used by the active pods)
CREATE ROLE smart_app_runtime_role NOLOGIN;

-- The runtime role CANNOT CREATE/DROP tables. It can only manipulate data.
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO smart_app_runtime_role;

-- Ensure default privileges assign correct rights to the runtime role when migrations run
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE smart_migration_role 
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO smart_app_runtime_role;

ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE smart_migration_role 
GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO smart_app_runtime_role;

-- 5. Service-Specific Identity Examples
-- Example for Identity Service
CREATE USER smart_identity_app WITH PASSWORD 'scram-sha-256...'; -- Injected via Vault
GRANT smart_app_runtime_role TO smart_identity_app;
-- Ensure smart_identity_app can only connect to smart_identity
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE smart_identity TO smart_identity_app;

-- Example for Payment Service
CREATE USER smart_payment_app WITH PASSWORD 'scram-sha-256...';
GRANT smart_app_runtime_role TO smart_payment_app;
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE smart_payment TO smart_payment_app;

-- 6. Read-Only Analytics Role (For ETL / Event polling if CDC is implemented)
CREATE ROLE smart_readonly_reporting_role NOLOGIN;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO smart_readonly_reporting_role;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE smart_migration_role 
GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO smart_readonly_reporting_role;

-- 7. Audit specific protections (Append Only Example)
-- Revoke UPDATE and DELETE on audit tables from the runtime role.
-- REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLE smart_audit.audit_events FROM smart_app_runtime_role;
</file>

<file path="database/redis/anpr/README.md">
# ANPR Redis Documentation

Redis in the ANPR Service provides ephemeral caching to accelerate operational throughput without compromising the authoritative integrity of PostgreSQL.

## Caching Strategies

### Camera Health & Config
- `anpr:camera:{cameraId}:health`
- `anpr:camera:{cameraId}:config`
**Purpose**: Avoid slamming the DB with heartbeat/config queries when evaluating thousands of plate recognition events per minute.

### Gate State
- `anpr:gate:{gateId}:state`
- `anpr:lane:{laneId}:state`
**Purpose**: Rapid validation of physical infrastructure status before producing authorization requests.

### Operations
- `anpr:authorization:{requestId}:state`
- `anpr:plate:{normalizedPlate}:recent`
- `anpr:border:{borderId}:state`
**Purpose**: `anpr:plate:{normalizedPlate}:recent` is critical for real-time duplicate rejection (debouncing duplicate recognitions of a stalled truck). 

## Failure Modes
If Redis falls offline, ANPR shifts query load to PostgreSQL.
**CRITICAL**: We never `FailOpen` gates just because Redis cache misses occur. Default `OperatingMode` is `FailClosed` or `ManualOnly`.
</file>

<file path="database/redis/audit/README.md">
# Audit Redis Documentation

Redis in the Audit Service provides ephemeral caching to manage idempotency, block abusive access, and cache integrity checkpoints.

## Caching Strategies

### Idempotency
- `audit:idempotency:{tenantId}:{operation}:{key}`
**Purpose**: Rapidly reject duplicate event submissions from mass integrations before inserting into PostgreSQL.

### Export / Search Rate Limiting
- `audit:rate-limit:{tenantId}:{userId}:{operation}`
**Purpose**: Limit outgoing audit mass-exports or heavy search queries. Prevents abusive actors from locking up PostgreSQL via heavy analytic scans.

### Integrity Verification Locks
- `audit:verification:{partition}`
**Purpose**: Track which worker is currently executing the cryptographic integrity check over a specific date partition to prevent redundant computational load.
</file>

# Integration Redis Documentation

Redis in the Integration Service provides ephemeral caching to accelerate operational throughput for circuit breaking and rate limiting without compromising the authoritative integrity of PostgreSQL.

## Caching Strategies

### Idempotency
- `integration:idempotency:{tenantId}:{operation}:{key}`
**Purpose**: Rapidly reject duplicate payloads before attempting PostgreSQL inserts.

### Webhook Deliveries
- `integration:webhook:{provider}:{eventId}`
**Purpose**: Duplicate event debouncing for massive inbound streams.

### Circuit Breakers
- `integration:circuit:{systemId}:{endpointId}`
**Purpose**: Rapid state transitions (`Open`, `HalfOpen`) for external provider connectivity.

### Rate Limiting
- `integration:rate-limit:{tenantId}:{endpointId}`
**Purpose**: Token Bucket or Sliding Window storage.
</file>

# Notification Redis Documentation

Redis in the Notification Service provides ephemeral caching to handle notification storms, deduping, rate limiting, and real-time state resolution without overwhelming the `smart_notification` PostgreSQL instance.

## Caching Strategies

### Storm Protection / Idempotency
- `notification:idempotency:{tenantId}:{operation}:{key}`
**Purpose**: Rapidly reject duplicate payloads before attempting PostgreSQL inserts (e.g. 500 identical GPS offline events).

### Unread States
- `notification:unread:{tenantId}:{userReference}`
**Purpose**: Instant retrieval of the unread badge count for UI clients.

### Rate Limiting
- `notification:rate-limit:{tenantId}:{userReference}:{channelType}`
**Purpose**: Limit outgoing SMS/Email per user/tenant to prevent abusive loops.

### Health
- `notification:provider-health:{provider}`
**Purpose**: Fast circuit breaker checks on external providers (SMS/Email Gateways).

<file path="database/redis/cache-policy.md">
# Cache Policy

- Implement explicit Cache-Aside strategy.
- Cache misses must query the authoritative PostgreSQL database.
- Treat Redis explicitly as non-authoritative acceleration.
- Implement invalidation via Outbox pattern (domain events). Do not assume cache updates persist simultaneously with SQL commits.
</file>

<file path="database/redis/failure-policy.md">
# Failure Policy

If Redis is down:
- Core operational reads must fallback to PostgreSQL (Fail-Open).
- Security verifications (e.g., ANPR gate authorization cache, Authentication replays) must Fail-Closed and explicitly deny access to prevent bypass.
</file>

<file path="database/redis/ha.md">
# High Availability (HA) Policy

- Production deployments require a managed Redis cluster or Redis Sentinel topology.
- Single-node Redis containers are strictly isolated to local Docker Compose workflows.
- Kubernetes operators ensure Pod Disruption Budgets (PDB) and health probes.
</file>

<file path="database/redis/key-naming.md">
# Redis Key Naming Policy

Keys must follow exactly:
`smart:{service}:{resource}:{scope}:{identifier}`

## Example
`smart:identity:session:{sessionId}`
`smart:fleet:vehicle:{tenantId}:{vehicleId}`

Arbitrary keys are strictly forbidden. Uncontrolled keys will be dropped by automated pipeline validations.
</file>

<file path="database/redis/lock-policy.md">
# Lock Policy

Locks must use `IDistributedLock` abstraction to safely coordinate access.

- Unique tokens and owner verification must be used.
- Atomic `NX` setting must enforce lock exclusivity.
- Do NOT issue bare `DEL` commands without confirming ownership token matches.
- All locks require aggressive TTLs. A crashed application must never permanently dead-lock a resource.
</file>

<file path="database/redis/monitoring.md">
# Monitoring Policy

- Export metrics natively to the observability stack.
- Track cache hit/miss ratio, connection limits, and eviction rates.
- Establish alerts for high memory fragmentation, unexpected hot keys, and replica disconnection.
</file>

<file path="database/redis/rate-limit-policy.md">
# Rate Limit Policy

Rate limits must leverage `IRateLimiter`.

- Sliding or fixed windows managed entirely via atomic Lua scripts inside Redis.
- Local in-memory limits are forbidden for distributed production enforcement.
- Internal service calls must not be collaterally rate-limited by public API protections. Use specific namespaces (e.g. `smart:system:ratelimit:ip:{ip}`).
</file>

<file path="database/redis/security.md">
# Redis Security Policy

- NO plaintext tokens, passwords, private keys, or raw payment details are allowed in Redis.
- Access Control Lists (ACLs) restrict microservices exclusively to their required namespaces (e.g., Fleet service -> `~smart:fleet:*`).
- TLS is mandatory in-transit.
- Secrets mapping for connecting to Redis must leverage Vault (`secret/platform/redis/services/{service}`).
</file>

<file path="database/redis/ttl-policy.md">
# TTL Policy

Every cached or state key in Redis MUST have a Time-To-Live (TTL).

- **Short-Lived (10-60s)**: Locks, Idempotency tokens, Replay Nonces, Gate Authorizations.
- **Medium (1-15m)**: GPS Latest, ANPR State, Dashboard Summaries.
- **Long (1-24h)**: User Sessions (governed by OAuth refresh policies), Reference Data.

No permanent keys are allowed without architect exemption.
</file>

<file path="docs/analytics/architecture.md">
# Analytics Architecture

The Enterprise Analytics Data Store operates independently from the operational microservices. It aggregates business intelligence asynchronously.

## Core Rules
1. **No Operational Querying**: Operational microservices (Identity, Payment, Fleet, Customs, etc.) never query `smart_analytics`.
2. **No Analytics Callbacks**: The Analytics service does not reach into operational databases to scrape data.
3. **Event Driven Ingestion**: Data arrives purely via RabbitMQ Domain Events (`TripCompletedEvent`, `PaymentSettledEvent`, etc.)

## Ingestion Pipeline
We utilize an Idempotent Consumer pattern via MassTransit.
When a domain event arrives, the consumer checks the Analytics database (e.g. `FactTrips`) by the operational Correlation ID (`TripId`). If it exists, it ignores it. If not, it transforms the data into Star Schema Dimensions/Facts and inserts it.

## Dimensions & Facts (Star Schema)
Data is structured utilizing SCD Type 2 tracking for dimensional changes over time (e.g., `DimTenant`, `DimVehicle`).
Facts (`FactTrip`, `FactPaymentOperational`) track numerical analysis tied by `DateKey` for rapid querying and dashboard rendering.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/ais-database.md">
# AIS / Vessel & Port Operations Database Architecture

## Overview
The `smart_ais` database utilizes **PostgreSQL** with the **PostGIS** extension to serve as the authoritative source for vessel lifecycle, port geometries, port-call assignments, and real-time operational boundaries across the Smart Trade & Logistics Corridor.

Simultaneously, `smart_ais_raw` operates in **MongoDB** to handle the unstructured, high-volume firehose of raw AIS provider messages. Finally, **Redis** caches latest known operational state for zero-latency queries.

## Boundary Enforcement
- **Fleet Boundary**: AIS tracks `Vessels`. It absolutely does not manage `Truck`, `Driver`, or `Vehicle` objects.
- **Corridor Boundary**: AIS manages the physical maritime tracking `Voyage`. The Corridor Trip master retains higher-order corridor coordination.
- **Customs & ECTN**: Identifiers link outward via `AisExternalReference`, but no customs tariffs or ECTN certificates exist inside the AIS boundary.

## PostGIS Integration
- Port definitions require PostGIS `geography(Point)` and `geometry(Geometry)`.
- Geofences evaluating vessel entry (`VesselPortEvent`) are natively backed by spatial evaluations natively tracked within Entity Framework via NetTopologySuite configurations.

## Multi-Tenancy & Security
- `TenantId` partitioning strictly prevents cross-tenant data leakage.
- Credentials for AIS data ingestion providers exist only in Vault (`secret/platform/ais/providers/*`), never in source or database strings.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/backup-recovery.md">
# Backup and Recovery Foundation

## Strategy
- **PostgreSQL**: Use `pg_dump` or `pg_basebackup` depending on the requirement (logical vs physical).
- **MongoDB**: Use `mongodump` for logical backups or snapshotting based on deployment.
- **Redis**: Rely on primary DBs for persistent state; AOF/RDB can be configured if explicitly required but primarily treated as ephemeral/cache.

## Requirements
- Backups must be timestamped and follow standard naming conventions.
- Retention policy must be legally aligned.
- Backups must be tested for restoration integrity regularly.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/corridor-database.md">
# Corridor / Trip / Route Management Database Architecture

## Overview
The `smart_corridor` database utilizes **PostgreSQL** coupled with **PostGIS** to provide highly accurate spatial operations across operational trade routes, enforcing strict milestone and checkpoint adherence across logistics corridors without duplicating the responsibilities of Fleet, GPS, or Customs databases.

## Spatial (PostGIS) Integration
- **Routes/Segments**: Managed via `geometry(LineString, 4326)` representing exact road paths.
- **Checkpoints/Milestones**: Managed via `geography(Point, 4326)` and `geometry(Polygon, 4326)` to allow exact proximity evaluations (e.g. `ST_DWithin` checks for checkpoint arrivals).
- **Spatial Indexing**: GiST indexes systematically applied to all geospatial columns.

## Boundary Enforcement
- GPS is responsible for emitting real-time telemetry coordinates. Corridor does *not* query GPS continuously; it consumes events to calculate `RouteDeviation`.
- Fleet retains all authority over the Truck, Driver, and Vehicle parameters. Corridor only captures references ensuring no out-of-sync master data.

## Immutable Data Strategies
- **ETA**: `TripEtaRecord` is an append-only time-series history log enabling BI tracking of corridor friction.
- **Versioning**: `RouteVersion`, `CorridorVersion`, and `TripVersion` prevent active operations from suffering silent mutations if administrators update reference geometry mid-transit.

## Caching (Redis)
- Uses key-stores (e.g. `corridor:trip:{tripId}:state`) strictly for read-model scaling, ensuring `smart_corridor` operates primarily as the authoritative operational datastore, decoupled from frontend querying loads.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/customs-database.md">
# Customs Management & Clearance Database Architecture

## Overview
The `smart_customs` database is the authoritative source for all things related to customs cases, assessments, tariff schedules, duty calculations, and cargo clearance. It intentionally avoids mirroring Declaration, ECTN, or Payment systems entirely to enforce a microservices boundary.

## ERD Core Groupings
- **CustomsCase** (Root Aggregate)
  - Connects to **CustomsReference** (Declarations, ECTN, etc.)
  - Connects to **CustomsAssessment** -> (**DutyAssessment**, **TaxAssessment**)
  - Connects to **CustomsValuation** -> (**CustomsValuationComponent**)
  - Connects to **InspectionOrder**, **CustomsHold**, **CustomsDecision**, **CustomsClearance**.
- **Configuration** (Version-Controlled Tariff/Rates Engine)
  - **TariffSchedule** -> **TariffScheduleVersion** -> **TariffItem**
  - **CustomsRate** -> **CustomsRateVersion**
  - **CustomsRule** -> **CustomsRuleVersion**
  - **ExemptionRule**

## Reproducibility & Immutability
All government rates (Tariff, Rules, Customs Rates) are heavily versioned (`VersionNumber`). When a historical `CustomsAssessment` is calculated, it directly snapshots the exact version IDs of the Tariff and Rules used. Subsequent publication of a new government rate (e.g. Duty changes from 10% to 15%) creates a new `TariffScheduleVersion` and does not silently alter historical assessments.

## Financial Precision
Because Customs deals heavily in international monetary conversions and weight, the following types were enforced mapped onto PostgreSQL `numeric(19,4)`:
- `CustomsValue`, `DutyAmount`, `CustomsChargesAmount`, `TotalAmount`
- `TaxableBase`, `Quantity`, `Rate`, `CalculatedAmount`
Exchange Rates use `numeric(19,6)`.

## Integration
Events like `CustomsCaseCreated` and `ClearanceApproved` use the `OutboxMessage` pattern to broadcast asynchronously to the gateway or other services.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/data-ownership.md">
# Data Ownership

## Principles
- **Every business service owns its own data.**
- NEVER create a shared business database schema between services.
- Data sharing MUST be done via REST APIs, API Gateway, or Integration Events (RabbitMQ/Event Bus).

## Anti-Patterns Forbidden
- Customs service accessing Fleet database directly.
- Payment service accessing Customs database directly.
- Direct operational database access from Analytics.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/database-standards.md">
# Database Standards

## Naming Conventions
- **C#**: `PascalCase`
- **PostgreSQL**: `snake_case`

## Primary Keys
- Use `uuid` (`Guid` in C#) for service-owned entity identifiers.
- Column name: `id`

## Foreign Keys
- Suffix with `_id` (e.g., `organization_id`)

## Money and Decimals
- Use PostgreSQL `NUMERIC(19,4)` for financial precision. NEVER use `float` or `double`.

## Timestamps
- `created_at_utc`
- `updated_at_utc`
- All persisted timestamps MUST be UTC.

## PostGIS
- Standard spatial reference: SRID 4326.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/declaration-database.md">
# Declaration Database Architecture

## ERD
The Cargo & Customs Declaration schema strictly enforces the regulatory and logistical transaction boundaries.

- **CustomsDeclaration** (1:M) **DeclarationVersion**, **DeclarationValidation**, **DeclarationSubmission**, **DeclarationDecision**, **DeclarationAmendment**, **DeclarationStatusHistory**, **DeclarationExternalReference**, **DeclarationIntegrationRecord**, **DeclarationReference**
- **DeclarationVersion** (1:M) **DeclarationParty**, **DeclarationCargo**, **DeclarationContainer**, **DeclarationTransport**, **DeclarationRoute**, **DeclarationDocument**
- **DeclarationParty** (1:M) **DeclarationPartyRole**
- **DeclarationCargo** (1:M) **DeclarationCargoItem**
- **DeclarationDocument** (1:M) **DeclarationDocumentVersion**

## Tenant Isolation
Multi-tenancy is native:
- `TenantId` exists on `CustomsDeclaration`, `DeclarationReference`, `DeclarationIntegrationRecord`, `IdempotencyRecord`, `DeclarationAuditEntry`.
- Unique constraints strictly scope applications: `UNIQUE (TenantId, DeclarationNumber)`.

## Data Consistency & Auditing
- **Optimistic Concurrency:** Enforced via EF Core `Version` column (`xmin` based) on `CustomsDeclaration`, `DeclarationVersion`, `DeclarationAmendment`, `DeclarationDocument`.
- **Audit Logs:** `DeclarationAuditEntry` stores immutable changes utilizing PostgreSQL `JSONB` for `BeforeJson` and `AfterJson`.
- **Financial/Quantitative Types:** `TotalGrossWeight`, `TotalNetWeight`, `TotalVolume`, `DeclaredValue`, `UnitPrice`, and `TotalValue` are strongly mapped to PostgreSQL `numeric(19,4)` to prevent floating-point precision loss.

## Document Storage
- Documents metadata is saved to PostgreSQL (`DeclarationDocument`).
- Actual binary data is assumed to be stored in an S3/MinIO compatible object store (`StorageObjectKey`).
- Enforces document immutability via `DeclarationDocumentVersion`.

## Integration Boundaries
- Safe cross-service messaging uses `OutboxMessage`.
- Incoming events rely on `InboxMessage` and `IdempotencyRecord` to guarantee exactly-once processing safely.
- **ECTN/Customs/Fleet/AIS Separation:** The declaration schema deliberately does NOT duplicate master definitions from ECTN, Customs Assessments, Payment Ledgers, or Fleet master tracking. It stores snapshots or reference IDs (`VehicleReference`, `EctnReference`) required for the specific transaction in time.
</file>

# ECTN Database Architecture

<file path="docs/database/fleet-database.md">
# Fleet & Vehicle Management Database Architecture

## Overview
The `smart_fleet` database is the authoritative source for fleet companies, vehicles (trucks/trailers), drivers, vehicle compliance, and driver verifications. 

It forms the foundational operational context for physical movement in the Smart Trade & Logistics Corridor.

## ERD Core Groupings
- **Core Assets** 
  - **FleetCompany** -> **Vehicle** / **Truck** / **Trailer** / **Driver**
- **Compliance & Credentialing**
  - **VehicleRegistration**, **VehicleCompliance**, **DriverLicense**, **DriverQualification**, **DriverCompliance**, **DriverVerification**
- **Operations & Assignments**
  - **DispatchOrder** (With **DispatchRequirement**)
  - **VehicleAssignment**, **DriverAssignment**, **TrailerAssignment**
- **History & Security**
  - **FleetHold** (Blocking states)
  - **FleetAuditEntry** (Traceability)
  - **StatusHistories**

## Multi-Tenancy & Isolation
All entities require a `TenantId`. Fleet operations are strictly siloed. A `FleetCompany` maps to a globally authenticated `OrganizationId` originating from the Identity database. Tenants cannot read or dispatch vehicles/drivers outside of their isolation boundary.

## Integration Boundaries (Strictly Enforced)
The Fleet Service must **NOT** replicate data belonging to:
- **Customs**: Tariffs, taxes, clearance rules, assessments.
- **ECTN**: Certificates.
- **GPS / Telematics**: GPS tables, live locations, telemetry data.
- **Payment**: Invoices, transactions.

Fleet stores only *external references* (e.g., `CustomsReleaseReference`, `DeclarationReference`) within the `DispatchOrder` or via `FleetExternalReference` to trigger readiness evaluations based on webhooks.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/gps-database.md">
# GPS & Telematics Database Architecture

## Overview
The `smart_gps` database utilizes **PostgreSQL** with the **PostGIS** extension to serve as the authoritative source for geospatial locations, geofencing, and vehicle tracking across the Smart Trade & Logistics Corridor. High-volume, flexible telemetry logs fall under the `smart_telemetry` **MongoDB** domain, while **Redis** powers real-time "latest location" queries for the Control Tower.

## PostGIS Architecture
- **SRID**: `4326` (WGS 84 coordinate system)
- **Data Types**: `geography(Point,4326)` for pure location points, `geometry(Geometry,4326)` for geofence boundaries to ensure accurate spherical math and containment validation.
- **Indexes**: `GiST` indexes are mapped across `VehicleLocation`, `GpsPosition`, `Geofence`, `GeofenceEvent`, and `TrackingAlert` allowing efficient `ST_Contains` and `ST_DWithin` spatial operations natively in the database.

## Boundary Enforcement
- **No Domain Leakage**: This database records locations for a `VehicleReference` string. It absolutely does **not** duplicate the Fleet master tables (Vehicle, Driver, Truck).
- **Corridor**: GPS publishes `RouteDeviationDetected` and `GeofenceEntered` events, but Corridor remains authoritative for the Trip Master. GPS tracks *what physically happened*.

## Commands & Telemetry
- Commands issued to IoT Gateways and Devices (`DeviceCommand`) are time-limited, JSONB payload structured, and emit a resulting `DeviceCommandResult`.
- Operational Telemetry (Odometer, Engine, Fuel) mappings exist for robust SQL query access when required.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/identity-database.md">
# Identity Database Architecture

## ERD
The Identity schema contains the following relationships:
- **Tenant** (1:M) **Organization**, (1:M) **User**, (1:M) **Role**, (1:M) **SecurityEvent**, (1:M) **IdentityAuditEntry**
- **User** (1:1) **UserSecurityState**, (1:M) **Session**, (1:M) **UserRole**, (1:M) **PasswordHistory**, (1:M) **EmailVerificationToken**, (1:M) **PasswordResetToken**, (1:M) **MfaConfiguration**
- **Role** (1:M) **UserRole**, (1:M) **RolePermission**
- **Permission** (1:M) **RolePermission**
- **Session** (1:M) **RefreshToken**
- **MfaConfiguration** (1:M) **MfaRecoveryCode**

## Tenant Isolation
- Tenants are the highest level of isolation.
- `tenant_id` exists on all major transactional/state tables.
- Constraints (`Unique(tenant_id, normalized_username)`, `Unique(tenant_id, organization_code)`) enforce this at the database level.
- Multi-tenancy is primarily enforced at the application level; RLS is not yet active but the schema structure fully supports future enablement.

## Security Model
- Passwords, Recovery Codes, Email Tokens, and Reset Tokens are **ONLY** stored as cryptographic hashes.
- `MfaConfiguration.SecretEncrypted` is symmetrically encrypted at the application level before database insertion.
- `SecurityEvent` and `IdentityAuditEntry` record all crucial identity actions and utilize PostgreSQL `JSONB` for extensible metadata without breaking the core relational model.
- `UserSecurityState` leverages an explicit `Version` concurrency token (`xmin` based) for optimistic locking to prevent race conditions during brute force scenarios or rapid concurrent logins.

## Retention Strategy
- Active configurations are never hard-deleted; `Status` flags (`Archived`, `Disabled`, `Revoked`) are used instead.
- Identity events (Security Events, Audit Entries) are append-only.
- Expiration (`ExpiresAtUtc`) acts as the active filter for tokens.

## Redis Integration
- The database is authoritative. Redis is solely used to cache roles, permissions, and active session verifications for performance. Redis is explicitly **not** the source of truth.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/indexing.md">
# Indexing Standards

## Rules
- Every index must have a justified reason based on query patterns.
- Common index columns: `tenant_id`, `created_at_utc`, `updated_at_utc`, `status`, `external_reference`.

## PostGIS
- Use `GiST` indexes for appropriate geometry/geography columns.

## Caution
Avoid excessive indexes to minimize write costs, storage, and maintenance overhead.
</file>

## Use Cases

## Avoid For
- Customs financial assessment source of truth
- Payment ledger
- Core identity

## Document Standards
- `_id`: String (UUID)
- `tenantId`
- `schemaVersion`
- `eventType`
- `source`
- `correlationId`
- `causationId`
- `occurredAtUtc`
- `receivedAtUtc`

## Indexing
- Based on query patterns.
- High-volume collections must consider: `tenantId`, `occurredAtUtc`, `receivedAtUtc`, `eventType`, `source`, `deviceId`.
- Use TTL index strategy where retention is appropriate, but never for legally retained records.

<file path="docs/database/payment-database.md">
# Payment Database Architecture

## Overview
The `smart_payment` database is the authoritative source for all things related to billing, invoicing, payments, ledgers, and transactions. It intentionally avoids mirroring Declaration, Customs, or ECTN systems entirely to enforce a microservices boundary. Instead, it relies on integration events (like `CustomsAssessmentApproved`) to trigger invoice creation.

## ERD Core Groupings
- **Billing** 
  - **Invoice** -> **InvoiceLineItem**
  - **CustomerAccount**
  - **Receipt**
- **Payment & Transaction**
  - **PaymentIntent** -> **PaymentTransaction**
- **Ledger**
  - **LedgerEntry** (Strictly Immutable, Hash-linked)
- **Configuration**
  - **PaymentGatewayConfiguration** -> **PaymentMethodConfiguration**

## Financial Immutability & Precision
Because the Payment microservice is essentially the financial ledger of the platform, the following types were enforced:
- **`numeric(19,4)`**: Used natively for all currency amounts (e.g. `AmountRequested`, `TotalAmount`, `SubtotalAmount`, `TaxAmount`, `AmountPaid`, `AmountDue`). This prevents fractional floating-point corruption.
- **Immutable Ledger**: The `LedgerEntry` entity represents a double-entry accounting log. It is explicitly configured in Entity Framework Core to restrict updates and cascading deletes, enforcing strict append-only immutability. Furthermore, a `Hash` and `PreviousHash` link can be used to cryptographically chain entries, preventing tampering.

## Integration
Events like `InvoicePaid` and `PaymentFailed` use the `OutboxMessage` pattern to broadcast asynchronously to the Customs, ECTN, or Declaration services.
Idempotency keys are explicitly enforced via `IdempotencyRecord` to guarantee that network retries during payment capture never double-charge a customer account.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/redis-architecture.md">
# Enterprise Redis Architecture

## Overview
Redis acts as a distributed runtime and acceleration layer for the Smart Trade & Logistics Corridor Platform. It provides fast access to idempotent checks, locks, and temporary state.

**CRITICAL TENET**: Redis MUST NEVER become the authoritative source of truth for business data.

## Namespace Structure
All keys must adhere to the `smart:{service}:{resource}:{scope}:{identifier}` naming convention.
- `service`: `identity`, `fleet`, `gps`, `corridor`, `controltower`, `system`, etc.
- `resource`: `vehicle`, `session`, `ratelimit`, `trip`, etc.
- `scope`: `tenantId` (Mandatory wherever applicable to enforce multi-tenancy isolation).
- `identifier`: The specific resource ID.

Example: `smart:fleet:vehicle:t1234:v5678`

## Serialization
Use JSON explicitly with a `schemaVersion` attached, avoiding arbitrary object types from the ORM.

## Fail-Open vs Fail-Closed
- **Fail-Open**: Configuration references, summary dashboards, generic health checks. If Redis fails, fall back directly to PostgreSQL.
- **Fail-Closed**: Idempotency gates, ANPR authorizations, lock acquisitions, replay protection (nonces). If Redis fails for these, reject the transaction gracefully.
</file>

<file path="docs/database/redis-standards.md">
# Redis Standards

## Use Cases
- Caching, distributed locks, idempotency, rate limiting, temporary session state.
- **MUST NOT be authoritative.** Systems must recover from PostgreSQL/MongoDB if Redis is lost.

## Key Naming Standard
- `service:resource:id`
- `service:tenant:resource:id`
- `service:cache:resource:key`
Examples: `identity:user:{id}:permissions`, `gps:vehicle:{id}:latest`

## Policies
- Define TTL policy for all entries.
- Never store secrets in Redis.
- Explicit distributed lock rules and idempotency key rules.
</file>

<file path="docs/database-security/SECURITY-BASELINE.md">
# ENTERPRISE DATABASE SECURITY BASELINE

## 1. Authentication & Vault Integration
All database credentials (`smart_identity_app`, `smart_payment_app`, etc.) are provisioned dynamically via **HashiCorp Vault**. 
- Secrets are never hardcoded in `appsettings.json` or committed to Git.
- PostgreSQL forces `scram-sha-256` password encryption.

## 2. TLS Encryption
All database connections (PostgreSQL, Redis) strictly require TLS. `sslmode=require` is enforced on all EF Core connection strings. Connections over plaintext are dropped at the Kubernetes Network layer.

## 3. Role Segregation (Least Privilege)
Applications operate using a restricted runtime role (`smart_app_runtime_role`).
- Runtime roles possess `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` only.
- Runtime roles **cannot** run DDL (`CREATE`, `DROP`, `ALTER`).
- Migrations run through isolated CI/CD pipelines using `smart_migration_role` which does not process user traffic.

## 4. Tenant Isolation (RLS vs EF Filters)
- **EF Core Global Query Filters**: Enforced automatically on all `DbContext` configurations ensuring `WHERE TenantId = @tenantId`. The `TenantId` is securely resolved from the authenticated JWT token, NOT the request payload.
- **Row Level Security (RLS)**: Staged for extremely sensitive bounded contexts (`smart_payment`, `smart_customs`).

## 5. Network Isolation
Kubernetes `NetworkPolicies` ensure that `smart_payment` can only be queried by the `payment-api` pod. 
No external ingress is allowed to port 5432 or 6379. Direct database console access requires connecting to the private VPC via VPN.

## 6. Audit Logging
`pgaudit` is configured on the primary cluster to record all structural DDL changes and permission escalation attempts. Routine SELECTs are ignored to preserve IOPS.
</file>

<file path="docs/database-security/THREAT-MODEL.md">
# DATABASE THREAT MODEL

| Threat | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation | Residual Risk |
|--------|--------|------------|------------|---------------|
| **SQL Injection** | Compromised Data | Low | Strict adherence to EF Core LINQ. Raw SQL parameterization. | Very Low |
| **Tenant Isolation Breach** | Data Leakage | Low | EF Core Global Query Filters (`TenantId`); JWT-driven identity. RLS on critical DBs. | Very Low |
| **Compromised App Pod** | Local DB Access | Medium | App roles lack DDL access (cannot DROP tables). Network Policies isolate DB to one pod. | Low |
| **Exposed Credentials** | DB Compromise | Low | Vault dynamic secrets. Secrets never logged or committed to Git. | Low |
| **Public Database Exposure** | DB Compromise | Low | Kubernetes internal VPC routing only. No public LoadBalancers attached to DB. | Very Low |
| **Malicious Insider (Admin)** | Data Theft/Tampering | Low | DB access audited via `pgaudit`. Read-only replicas used for analysis. | Medium |
| **Ransomware / Backup Deletion**| Data Loss | Low | S3 backups are versioned and logically separated from primary DB cluster. | Low |
</file>

<file path="docs/deployment/PRODUCTION-ARCHITECTURE.md">
# Production Architecture & Kubernetes Hardening

## 1. Environments & Namespaces
- `platform-dev`
- `platform-test`
- `platform-staging`
- `platform-performance`
- `platform-production`

## 2. Kubernetes Network Policies (Default DENY)
- **Ingress**: External traffic is ONLY permitted to the YARP API Gateway Pods.
- **Service-to-Service**: Gateway may route to domain services. Domain services may communicate with internal Redis, PostgreSQL, and RabbitMQ exclusively via explicitly allowed egress rules.
- **Public Exposure**: PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ are strictly isolated to internal cluster networking.

## 3. Pod Security Standards
All application pods enforce the **Restricted** profile:
- `runAsNonRoot: true`
- `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` (where possible)
- Drops all default Linux capabilities.

## 4. Autoscaling (HPA) & Disruption (PDB)
- **HPA**: Configured for Gateway, Control Tower BFF, and high-volume consumers (GPS/ANPR) based on Phase 15.7 load test targets.
- **PDB**: Minimum availability set to ensure rolling updates or node drains do not drop critical workloads below 50% capacity.
</file>

<file path="docs/deployment/PRODUCTION-DEPLOYMENT-RUNBOOK.md">
# Production Deployment Runbook

## Deployment Execution (GitOps via ArgoCD)
1. **Approval**: CI pipeline successfully updates the GitOps manifest repo. Pull Request to `production` branch is approved by Tech Lead.
2. **Sync**: ArgoCD detects the change on the `production` branch and triggers a sync.
3. **Rollout**: Kubernetes executes a RollingUpdate. 
4. **Probes**: Readiness probes hold traffic until new pods initialize dependencies (Redis, Postgres).
5. **Database Migrations**: Executed as a pre-sync hook job or dedicated init-container strategy. Must be backward-compatible with the running N-1 application version.
6. **Smoke Test**: Automated post-deploy validation (Auth check, critical API health).
</file>

<file path="docs/deployment/ROLLBACK-RUNBOOK.md">
# Rollback Runbook

## ArgoCD Rollback
1. **Git Revert**: The primary rollback mechanism is to revert the GitOps repository commit to the previous stable state.
2. **Sync**: ArgoCD detects the revert and syncs Kubernetes back to the N-1 image digest.

## Database Rollback Considerations
- **CRITICAL**: Application rollbacks MUST NOT trigger automatic database schema down-migrations. Down-migrations often involve destructive data loss.
- **Backward Compatibility**: Migrations must follow Expand/Contract patterns so that N-1 code can safely run against N schema during an emergency rollback.
</file>

<file path="docs/devsecops/DEVSECOPS-RUNBOOK.md">
# DevSecOps Runbook

## CI Pipeline Stages (Quality Gates)
1. **Checkout & Secret Scan**: Gitleaks fails build if secrets are detected.
2. **Build & Unit Tests**: .NET `dotnet build` and `dotnet test`.
3. **SAST**: Static analysis fails on Critical/High findings.
4. **Container Build**: Multi-stage Dockerfile builds minimal runtime image.
5. **Trivy Container Scan**: Fails pipeline on Critical/High CVEs.
6. **SBOM Generation**: Output pushed as Jenkins artifact.
7. **Image Push**: Secure push to Private Registry.
8. **GitOps Update**: Jenkins commits updated image tag/digest to the ArgoCD target repository.

## Vault Secret Rotation Strategy
- Database credentials rotated via Vault Dynamic Secrets.
- JWT Signing keys rotated with overlapping validation windows to prevent sudden session invalidation.
</file>

<file path="docs/disaster-recovery/DR-RUNBOOK.md">
# DISASTER RECOVERY RUNBOOK

This runbook outlines the operational steps taken during a SEV-1 catastrophic failure (e.g., regional outage, severe cluster failure, mass ransomware event).

## 1. Incident Declaration
If PagerDuty alerts fire for `PostgreSQL Primary Unreachable` across multiple domains, declare a SEV-1 incident in Slack (`#incident-sev1-database`).

## 2. Identify Failure & Freeze Writes
Identify if the outage is hardware, network, or logical data corruption.
**If Data Corruption:**
- Scale all API Deployments down to `0` to prevent cascading corruption and stop further data ingestion.
  ```bash
  kubectl scale deploy -l tier=api --replicas=0 -n smart-trade-prod
  ```

## 3. Provision Recovery Environment
If the primary cluster is permanently lost, instantiate the DR Terraform cluster.
- Apply Infrastructure (`terraform apply -var="env=dr"`)
- Ensure HashiCorp Vault is unsealed in the new region.

## 4. Execute Restore Sequence
Follow the exact dependency chain established in `DATABASE-DEPENDENCY-MAP.md`:
1. **Unseal Vault & Secrets**
2. **Restore PostgreSQL `smart_identity` (Auth Core)**
3. **Restore PostgreSQL `smart_payment`, `smart_customs` (Financial Core)**
4. **Restore Messaging (RabbitMQ state)**
5. **Restore Operational Domains (Fleet, GPS, Corridor)**
6. **Flush & Rebuild Redis** (from events)

## 5. Post-Restore Validation
- **Tenant Isolation:** Run API smoke tests ensuring Tenant A tokens cannot read Tenant B endpoints.
- **Financials:** Run Ledger Reconciliation checks on `smart_payment`.
- **Idempotency:** Verify Inbox/Outbox records to ensure RabbitMQ message replay won't duplicate customs assessments.

## 6. Resume Operations & Post-Incident Review
1. Scale APIs back up incrementally.
2. Monitor Application APM for Error Spikes.
3. Close the SEV-1.
4. Schedule a Post-Incident Review (PIR) to document the exact Data Loss Window and actual Time-To-Recover vs RTO.
</file>

<file path="docs/disaster-recovery/RESTORE-RUNBOOK.md">
# DATABASE RESTORE RUNBOOK

This runbook describes the explicit steps to restore a PostgreSQL database (e.g. `smart_payment`) from an S3 backup, covering both Logical Dumps and Point-In-Time-Recovery (PITR).

## Prerequisites
- Access to the target Kubernetes Cluster (`kubectl`).
- Appropriate Vault access roles to decrypt the PostgreSQL and S3 credentials.

---

## Scenario A: Logical Restore (pg_dump recovery)
*Use when a non-critical database needs a full overwrite or a specific missing table needs recovery.*

1. **Locate the Backup in S3**
   ```bash
   aws s3 ls s3://smart-trade-backups-bucket/postgres/smart_payment/
   ```
2. **Download and Verify Checksum**
   ```bash
   aws s3 cp s3://smart-trade-backups-bucket/postgres/smart_payment/20260921_020000/smart_payment_20260921_020000.sql.gz .
   aws s3 cp s3://smart-trade-backups-bucket/postgres/smart_payment/20260921_020000/smart_payment_20260921_020000.sql.gz.sha256 .
   sha256sum -c smart_payment_20260921_020000.sql.gz.sha256
   ```
   *If `FAILED`, abort the recovery and locate a non-corrupted backup.*

3. **Restore to Isolated Database**
   ```bash
   gunzip -c smart_payment_20260921_020000.sql.gz | psql -h isolated-db-instance -U postgres -d smart_payment
   ```
4. **Validate Data**
   Run the test matrix queries (e.g., verifying Payment counts, ledger balance constraints).

---

## Scenario B: Point-In-Time-Recovery (PITR) using pgBackRest
*Use when critical financial/identity databases suffer from accidental truncation or corruption and must be restored to a specific minute before the failure.*

1. **Identify the exact failure timestamp (UTC)**
   Let's assume the failure occurred at `2026-09-21 14:32:00`. We want to restore to `14:31:59`.

2. **Execute pgBackRest Restore Command** (Running inside the Postgres pod or a sidecar recovery pod)
   ```bash
   pgbackrest --stanza=smart_payment --type=time --target="2026-09-21 14:31:59" --delta restore
   ```

3. **Startup PostgreSQL**
   The database will automatically replay the WAL logs from S3 until it reaches the exact target timestamp.

4. **Verify Constraints and Relationships**
   - Check the `smart_payment` `Outbox` table. Are there records that were processed between `14:31:59` and now? These may need replay.
</file>

<file path="docs/dr/PHASE-15.8-BACKUP-STRATEGY.md">
# Backup and Disaster Recovery Strategy

## 1. PostgreSQL (Transactional Data)
- **Type**: Logical backups (pg_dump) + WAL archiving (pgBackRest/Barman).
- **Frequency**: Continuous WAL archiving. Full backup daily.
- **Retention**: 30 days hot, 7 years cold (Audit/Customs compliance).
- **PITR**: Enabled. Can restore to any second within the 30-day window.

## 2. MinIO (Object Storage - Evidence/Documents)
- **Type**: Bucket replication + Versioning.
- **Frequency**: Continuous active-active replication to standby cluster.
- **Retention**: Indefinite for Customs Evidence (ANPR images, manifests).

## 3. Redis (Cache / Backplane)
- **Type**: Ephemeral (No backup required).
- **Recovery**: System designed to safely degrade and rebuild cache from authoritative PostgreSQL data upon Redis restart.

## 4. RabbitMQ (Messaging)
- **Type**: Configuration backup (Definitions JSON).
- **Data Recovery**: Queues are durable, but in a catastrophic broker loss, services rely on the EF Core Outbox table in PostgreSQL to republish unpublished integration events.
</file>

<file path="docs/resilience/PHASE-15.8-RESILIENCE-INVENTORY.md">
# Platform Resilience Inventory

## 1. Retry Policies (Polly)
- **Database (EF Core)**: Uses `EnableRetryOnFailure()` for transient SQL connection errors.
- **Messaging (MassTransit)**: Configured with `UseMessageRetry(r => r.Interval(3, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)))`.
- **External Providers (Payment)**: Uses Exponential Backoff with Jitter for external HTTP calls to prevent retry storms on provider failure.

## 2. Circuit Breakers
- **API Gateway (YARP)**: Rejects traffic to backend pools that fail consecutive health checks, failing fast for the client.
- **Customs to Fleet**: Circuit breaker triggers after 50% failure rate over 30 seconds, returning degraded cache state where permitted.

## 3. Data Durability & Idempotency
- **Outbox Pattern**: All 14 microservices use EF Core Outbox (`OutboxMessage.cs`) to guarantee atomicity between Postgres business state and RabbitMQ event publishing.
- **Inbox Pattern**: Consumers check `InboxMessage` table to ensure duplicate RabbitMQ deliveries (at-least-once guarantee) do not result in double ledger entries or duplicate customs clearance.

## 4. Kubernetes Resilience
- **Probes**: Liveness (TCP), Readiness (HTTP `/health`), and Startup probes configured for all API pods.
- **PodDisruptionBudget (PDB)**: Ensures minimum 1 replica available during node drains.
</file>

<file path="docs/security/PHASE-15.6-SECURITY-BASELINE.md">
# Phase 15.6 Security Baseline

## 1. Zero Trust Architecture
The Smart Trade & Logistics Corridor Platform operates on a strict Zero Trust model. Internal network location (e.g., executing within the Kubernetes cluster) does NOT confer trust. 

All service-to-service communication, including MassTransit/RabbitMQ integration events and internal REST API calls, MUST carry cryptographic proof of identity and tenant context (e.g., `X-Correlation-ID`, `X-Tenant-Id` derived from a validated OAuth2 JWT).

## 2. Trust Boundaries
- **Untrusted (Internet)**: Driver Mobile App, ANPR Cameras, External Payment Providers, Browser Clients.
- **Verification (Edge)**: API Gateway (YARP). Validates JWT signature, expiration, and issuer. Rejects malformed requests before routing.
- **Authorization (BFF & Domain)**: Control Tower BFF, Domain Microservices. Evaluate claims (Role, Permission, Tenant) against the requested resource. Frontend authorization (`RequirePermission.tsx`) is strictly for UX, not security.
- **Core (Database/Event Bus)**: PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ. Protected by mutual TLS (mTLS) and least-privilege service accounts.

## 3. Structural SAST Findings (from Scaffolding)
- `IIntegrationEvent.cs`: **PASS**. Strictly requires `TenantId`, preventing ambient cross-tenant contamination in the event stream.
- `RequirePermission.tsx`: **PASS**. Correctly assumes frontend is not the security boundary.
- `ControlTowerHub.cs`: **PASS**. Correctly partitions WebSocket connections by `Tenant_{tenantId}` during `OnConnectedAsync` to prevent SignalR event leakage.
</file>

<file path="docs/security/threat-model.md">
# Platform Threat Model

## 1. Threat Actors
- **External Attacker**: Attempts API enumeration, credential stuffing, and DDoS against the API Gateway.
- **Malicious Tenant (Logistics/Trader)**: Attempts IDOR/BOLA to access competing tenant's cargo data, customs holds, or GPS telemetry.
- **Compromised GPS/ANPR Device**: Attempts to spoof location data or fabricate gate authorizations to bypass customs checks.
- **Insider Threat**: Unauthorized attempts by internal users (e.g., Driver) to elevate privileges to Logistics Admin or Customs Officer.

## 2. Threat Categories (STRIDE)
- **Spoofing**: Faking ANPR events to clear a border. *Mitigation*: mTLS and cryptographic device credentials at the ingestion API.
- **Tampering**: Altering Customs Assessment rates (e.g., from 15% to 10%) via intercepted React payload. *Mitigation*: Backend calculates authoritative values from read-only Government Configuration; ignores client-supplied duty rates.
- **Repudiation**: Driver denying receipt of goods. *Mitigation*: Immutable Audit trails and EF Core Outbox pattern ensuring DeliveryConfirmed events are durable.
- **Information Disclosure**: Tenant A reading Tenant B's SignalR feed. *Mitigation*: Strict SignalR group isolation in `ControlTowerHub.cs`.
- **Denial of Service**: High-frequency GPS flooding. *Mitigation*: YARP Rate Limiting and Payload Size constraints.
- **Elevation of Privilege**: Driver attempting to hit `/api/v1/government/tariff`. *Mitigation*: Strict JWT Role and Permission claims validated at the Domain Controller level.
</file>

</file>

<file path="frontend/web/src/app/auth/RequirePermission.tsx">
import React from 'react';
import { Navigate, useLocation } from 'react-router-dom';

interface RequirePermissionProps {
  children: JSX.Element;
  requiredPermission?: string;
  requiredRole?: string;
  requiredTenantAccess?: string;
}

// Mock auth hook for scaffolding
const useAuth = () => {
  return {
    isAuthenticated: true,
    user: {
      roles: ['CUSTOMS_OFFICER'],
      permissions: ['customs.configuration.read'],
      tenantType: 'GOVERNMENT',
    },
    isLoading: false,
  };
};

export const RequirePermission: React.FC<RequirePermissionProps> = ({
  children,
  requiredPermission,
  requiredRole,
  requiredTenantAccess,
}) => {
  const { isAuthenticated, user, isLoading } = useAuth();
  const location = useLocation();

  if (isLoading) return <div>Loading session...</div>;

  if (!isAuthenticated) {
    return <Navigate to="/login" state={{ from: location }} replace />;
  }

  if (requiredRole && !user.roles.includes(requiredRole)) {
    return <Navigate to="/unauthorized" replace />;
  }

  if (requiredPermission && !user.permissions.includes(requiredPermission)) {
    return <Navigate to="/unauthorized" replace />;
  }

  if (requiredTenantAccess && user.tenantType !== requiredTenantAccess) {
    return <Navigate to="/unauthorized" replace />;
  }

  return children;
};
</file>

<file path="frontend/web/src/app/RequireAuth.tsx">
import React from 'react';
import { Navigate, Outlet, useLocation } from 'react-router-dom';
// import { useAuthStore } from '../stores/authStore'; // Imaginary global state store

export const RequireAuth: React.FC = () => {
  // const { isAuthenticated, isInitializing } = useAuthStore();
  const isAuthenticated = true; // Mocked for scaffolding
  const isInitializing = false;
  const location = useLocation();

  if (isInitializing) {
    return <div>Loading authentication state...</div>;
  }

  if (!isAuthenticated) {
    return <Navigate to="/login" state={{ from: location }} replace />;
  }

  return <Outlet />;
};

export const RequirePermission: React.FC<{ permission: string }> = ({ permission }) => {
  // const { permissions } = useAuthStore();
  const permissions = ['control-tower.read']; // Mocked
  const hasPermission = permissions.includes(permission);

  if (!hasPermission) {
    return <Navigate to="/403" replace />;
  }

  return <Outlet />;
};

interface ControlTowerOverview {

  vehiclesLive: number;
  vehiclesStale: number;
  pendingCustoms: number;
  openAlerts: number;
}

export const useControlTowerOverview = () => {

    queryKey: ['control-tower', 'overview'],
    queryFn: async () => {
      const response = await api.get('/control-tower/overview');
      return response.data;

    // but we can also set a slow polling interval as a fallback

apiClient.interceptors.request.use((config) => {

import { BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Navigate } from 'react-router-dom';

<file path="mobile/driver/lib/core/networking/api_client.dart">
import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
import 'package:flutter_secure_storage/flutter_secure_storage.dart';
import 'package:uuid/uuid.dart';

class ApiClient {
  final Dio _dio;
  final FlutterSecureStorage _secureStorage;
  static const String _tokenKey = 'access_token';
  static const String _refreshTokenKey = 'refresh_token';

  ApiClient({required String baseUrl, required FlutterSecureStorage secureStorage})
      : _secureStorage = secureStorage,
        _dio = Dio(BaseOptions(
          baseUrl: baseUrl,
          connectTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 15),
          receiveTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 15),
        )) {
    _dio.interceptors.add(_createAuthInterceptor());
    _dio.interceptors.add(_createRetryInterceptor());
  }

  Interceptor _createAuthInterceptor() {
    return InterceptorsWrapper(
      onRequest: (options, handler) async {
        final token = await _secureStorage.read(key: _tokenKey);
        if (token != null) {
          options.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer $token';
        }
        
        // Inject Idempotency-Key for POST/PUT requests
        if (options.method == 'POST' || options.method == 'PUT') {
          options.headers['Idempotency-Key'] = const Uuid().v4();
        }
        
        // Inject CorrelationId
        options.headers['X-Correlation-ID'] = const Uuid().v4();
        
        return handler.next(options);
      },
      onError: (DioException e, handler) async {
        if (e.response?.statusCode == 401) {
          // Attempt token refresh logic here
          // If refresh fails, clear session and throw specific AuthException
          await _secureStorage.delete(key: _tokenKey);
          await _secureStorage.delete(key: _refreshTokenKey);
          // throw AuthException('Session expired');
        }
        return handler.next(e);
      },
    );
  }

  Interceptor _createRetryInterceptor() {
    return InterceptorsWrapper(
      onError: (DioException e, handler) {
        // Implement exponential backoff for 5xx and 429
        if (e.response?.statusCode == 429 || (e.response?.statusCode ?? 0) >= 500) {
           // Queue for retry logic
        }
        return handler.next(e);
      }
    );
  }
}
</file>

<file path="mobile/driver/lib/core/synchronization/offline_queue.dart">
import 'dart:convert';
import 'package:uuid/uuid.dart';

enum OfflineEventStatus { Pending, Sending, Succeeded, Failed, DeadLetter }

class OfflineEvent {
  final String localId;
  final String eventType;
  final String aggregateType;
  final String aggregateId;
  final DateTime createdAtUtc;
  final Map<String, dynamic> payload;
  int retryCount;
  OfflineEventStatus status;
  String? errorCode;

  OfflineEvent({
    required this.eventType,
    required this.aggregateType,
    required this.aggregateId,
    required this.payload,
  })  : localId = const Uuid().v4(),
        createdAtUtc = DateTime.now().toUtc(),
        retryCount = 0,
        status = OfflineEventStatus.Pending;
}

abstract class IOfflineQueueRepository {
  Future<void> enqueue(OfflineEvent event);
  Future<List<OfflineEvent>> getPendingEvents();
  Future<void> updateEventStatus(String localId, OfflineEventStatus status);
  Future<void> incrementRetry(String localId);
}

class OfflineSyncEngine {
  final IOfflineQueueRepository _repository;
  // final ApiClient _apiClient;

  OfflineSyncEngine(this._repository);

  Future<void> syncPendingEvents() async {
    final pending = await _repository.getPendingEvents();
    for (var event in pending) {
      try {
        await _repository.updateEventStatus(event.localId, OfflineEventStatus.Sending);
        // Simulate API call using ApiClient
        // await _apiClient.post('/api/sync', data: event.payload);
        await _repository.updateEventStatus(event.localId, OfflineEventStatus.Succeeded);
      } catch (e) {
        // Handle permanent vs transient errors
        await _repository.incrementRetry(event.localId);
        // If max retries, move to DeadLetter
      }
    }
  }
}
</file>

<file path="scripts/database/backup_postgres.sh">
#!/bin/bash
set -eo pipefail

echo "Starting logical backup of all databases..."
TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
BACKUP_DIR="/backups"
DB_LIST="smart_identity smart_ectn smart_declaration smart_customs smart_payment smart_fleet smart_gps smart_corridor smart_anpr smart_integration smart_notification smart_audit smart_analytics"

# Requires aws-cli to be installed in the pod/container running this
for DB in $DB_LIST; do
  echo "Backing up $DB..."
  DUMP_FILE="${BACKUP_DIR}/${DB}_${TIMESTAMP}.sql.gz"
  
  # Perform logical backup
  pg_dump -h $PGHOST -U $PGUSER -d $DB | gzip > $DUMP_FILE
  
  # Generate checksum
  CHECKSUM=$(sha256sum $DUMP_FILE | awk '{print $1}')
  echo "$CHECKSUM" > "${DUMP_FILE}.sha256"
  
  # Upload to S3
  echo "Uploading $DB backup to S3..."
  aws s3 cp $DUMP_FILE s3://${S3_BUCKET}/postgres/${DB}/${TIMESTAMP}/
  aws s3 cp "${DUMP_FILE}.sha256" s3://${S3_BUCKET}/postgres/${DB}/${TIMESTAMP}/
  
  echo "Completed backup for $DB (Checksum: $CHECKSUM)"
done

echo "All logical backups completed successfully."
</file>

<file path="services/ais-vessel/AisVessel.Api/Controllers/BerthAllocationsController.cs">
using System;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using MediatR;
using AisVessel.Application.Commands;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;

namespace AisVessel.Api.Controllers;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/v1/ais/berth-allocations")]
[Authorize]
public class BerthAllocationsController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly IMediator _mediator;

    public BerthAllocationsController(IMediator mediator)
    {
        _mediator = mediator;
    }

    [HttpPost]
    [Authorize(Policy = "ais.berth.allocate")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> AllocateBerth([FromBody] AllocateBerthCommand command)
    {
        if (User.HasClaim(c => c.Type == "tenantId"))
        {
            command.TenantId = Guid.Parse(User.FindFirst("tenantId").Value);
        }

        var portCallId = await _mediator.Send(command);
        return Ok(new { PortCallId = portCallId, Status = "BerthAllocated" });
    }
}

<file path="services/ais-vessel/AisVessel.Application/Commands/AllocateBerthCommand.cs">
using System;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using MediatR;
using AisVessel.Domain.Entities;
using AisVessel.Domain.Enums;
using AisVessel.Infrastructure.Persistence;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

namespace AisVessel.Application.Commands;

public class AllocateBerthCommand : IRequest<Guid>
{
    public Guid TenantId { get; set; }
    public Guid PortCallId { get; set; }
    public Guid BerthId { get; set; }
}

public class AllocateBerthCommandHandler : IRequestHandler<AllocateBerthCommand, Guid>
{
    private readonly AisDbContext _context;

    public AllocateBerthCommandHandler(AisDbContext context)
    {
        _context = context;
    }

    public async Task<Guid> Handle(AllocateBerthCommand request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var portCall = await _context.PortCalls
            .FirstOrDefaultAsync(p => p.Id == request.PortCallId && p.TenantId == request.TenantId, cancellationToken);
            
        if (portCall == null) throw new InvalidOperationException("PortCall not found.");
        
        var berth = await _context.Berths
            .FirstOrDefaultAsync(b => b.Id == request.BerthId && b.TenantId == request.TenantId, cancellationToken);
            
        if (berth == null) throw new InvalidOperationException("Berth not found.");

        if (portCall.Status != PortCallStatus.AwaitingBerth)
        {
            throw new InvalidOperationException("PortCall must be AwaitingBerth to allocate a berth.");
        }

        portCall.AdvanceState(PortCallStatus.BerthAllocated);
        
        // Example: in full implementation, we'd add the BerthAllocation entity here,
        // evaluate the IBerthAllocationService rules to ensure Length/Draft match,
        // and raise a BerthAllocatedIntegrationEvent via Outbox.
        
        await _context.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);

        return portCall.Id;
    }
}

<file path="services/ais-vessel/AisVessel.Domain/Entities/PortZone.cs">
using System;
using NetTopologySuite.Geometries;
using AisVessel.Domain.Enums;

namespace AisVessel.Domain.Entities;

public class PortZone
{
    public Guid Id { get; private set; }
    public Guid TenantId { get; private set; }
    public string PortCode { get; private set; }
    public PortZoneType Type { get; private set; }
    public string Name { get; private set; }
    
    // PostGIS Geometry for Polygon/MultiPolygon
    public Geometry Boundary { get; private set; }
    
    public bool Active { get; private set; }
    public DateTime CreatedAt { get; private set; }
    public DateTime? UpdatedAt { get; private set; }
    public byte[] Version { get; private set; }

    protected PortZone() { }

    public PortZone(
        Guid tenantId,
        string portCode,
        string name,
        PortZoneType type,
        Geometry boundary)
    {
        if (boundary == null) throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(boundary));
        
        // Ensure SRID is set
        if (boundary.SRID == 0) boundary.SRID = 4326;

        Id = Guid.NewGuid();
        TenantId = tenantId;
        PortCode = portCode;
        Name = name;
        Type = type;
        Boundary = boundary;
        Active = true;
        CreatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
    }
}
